verdicts.reason: I could not reach any primary source: WebFetch failed with DNS errors on every host and the WebSearch budget was used up. The repo evidence points both ways. The finding misreads data/visadocs.yaml: its `B-1>D-4-1` exception is for German nationals only (`countries: [DE]`, the general German B-1 rule), so it does not show that B-1 holders in general can change to D-4-1 in Korea. The author's own choice of `abroad: true` for D-4-1 next to `abroadFor: notified` for D-2 on the same lines, and another audit agent's quote of the same guideline (D-4-1 허가대상 = '외국인등록 후 국내에 체류하고 있는 자', excluding only D-3/E-9/E-10/G-1), both argue against the claim. Against that, the 2026.9.18 D-4-1 change list asks for the ARC only from '소지자', which hints that some applicants are not registered. If a primary source does confirm the claim, the fix is expressible as written: reuse the four-language D-2 note and keep C-3-9 as `abroad: true`.

verdicts.reason: Part of the claim is right: the manual documents an in-Korea change to F-4 from short-term statuses, and the map shows only a plane icon with no note. But the finding's own quote makes the change conditional ('에 한하여'): only when the proof documents are issued in Korea or can be checked in the system, or for CIS ethnic Koreans who held C-3-8/H-2/F-4 before. So applying from abroad stays the default. The repo encodes exactly this as `abroad: true` plus the in-Korea exceptions in data/visadocs.yaml (B-1>F-4, B-2>F-4, C-3-1>F-4, C-3-4>F-4, C-3-9>F-4), which the visa-docs page shows as '✈*'. The proposed plain `- F-4` would turn the default around and also stop visadocs.js from showing those exceptions, because withExceptions() only runs on abroad moves. The finding also missed C-3-4 (line 189). In this engine a move's note replaces the visa's 'how' text, so the note has to repeat F-4's requirements.

  abroad: true

From a short-term stay this is normally a new visa from abroad; you can change in Korea if your proof of Korean descent is issued in Korea or can be checked in the immigration system, or if you are an ethnic Korean from a CIS country who held C-3-8, H-2 or F-4 before.', ru: <translate>, uz: <translate>, uz-cyrl: <translate>}

verdicts.reason: The claim is right that the 2026.9.18 manual documents in-Korea changes to E-7-1 for short-term holders, transcribed in data/visadocs.yaml: a foreign-school teacher from any status; high-tech specialists who entered visa-free or hold a non-work visa, with a ministry recommendation; and, from B-1/B-2 only, Jeju international-school staff. The map's edges mention none of them. But these are exceptions: the general change group in the same chapter is registered D-1, D-2, D-4~D-10 and E-1~E-6 holders. So `abroad: true` is the correct default, and the finding's fix contradicts itself (it drops the flag but says 'Normally a new visa from abroad'). Dropping the flag would also stop the visa-docs page from showing these exceptions ('✈*'). The note must restate E-7-1's 'how', because a move note replaces it, and the Jeju clause applies only to B-1 and B-2.

verdicts.reason: The claim is right. The 2026.9.18 F-6 chapter, as transcribed in data/visadocs.yaml (B-1>F-6-1 … C-4>F-6-1), allows short-term holders to change to F-6-1 in Korea when leaving is unavoidable because of pregnancy, childbirth or raising the couple's own (not adopted) child. Another verifier, using a secondary source (f-6.co.kr), found short-term statuses (C-3, C-4, B-1, B-2) listed as restricted, so `abroad: true` is the correct default. Keeping the plane and adding a note fits the engine. But the proposed note has only English and would replace F-6-1's 'how' text on these edges: in howTo() a move note takes the place of the visa's 'how'. Readers would then lose the ₩25.2M income, Korean-language and housing requirements, because F-6-1 has no `income:` field. The note must restate them and needs all four languages.
